# The Jev API cannot be verified with the credential on this machine

Probed on 23 September 2026 against POST https://thejevai.com/v1/systemone, one throwaway question
("Is the sky blue?") carrying no repository content.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `Authorization: Bearer <JEV_AI_API_KEY>` | 401 `{"code":-1,"message":"Invalid API key."}` |
| `Authorization: <JEV_AI_API_KEY>` | 401 `{"code":-1,"message":"Invalid API key."}` |
| `x-api-key: <JEV_AI_API_KEY>` | 401 `{"code":-1,"message":"Please sign in to use the playground."}` |
| `api-key: <JEV_AI_API_KEY>` | 401 `{"code":-1,"message":"Please sign in to use the playground."}` |

What this establishes: the endpoint exists, it authenticates through the Authorization header, and
the credential in this shell (`JEV_AI_API_KEY`, 60 characters, prefix `vck`) is not valid for it.
The two distinct 401 messages separate "no credential at all" from "credential rejected", so the
header form is confirmed even though the key is not.

What it does not establish: the request body, the response body, how a `noul` answer carries its
probability, or how a `score` question returns per-option probabilities. Those are the contract the
harness has to parse, and inventing them would be exactly the failure CLAUDE.md rule 6 names.

Decision taken rather than left open: build the decision layer with a transport seam and the
human-fallback path, both fully tested, and leave the live call unverified until a valid Jev
credential exists. The fallback path is not a stopgap; the ticket requires it in its own right, and
it is what the harness uses whenever the API is unavailable.
